records.title: BRCA2 C-terminal clamp restructures RAD51 dimers to bind B-DNA for replication fork stability
records.abstract: Tumor suppressor protein breast cancer susceptibility protein 2 (BRCA2) acts with RAD51 in replication fork protection (FP) and homology-directed DNA-break repair (HDR). Critical for cancer etiology and therapy resistance, the BRCA2 C terminus was thought to stabilize recombinogenic RAD51 after the assembly of ATP-extended RAD51 filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). Here, the detailed crystal structure of the human BRCA2 C-terminal interaction domain (TR2 interface [TR2i]) complexed with ATP-bound RAD51 prior to DNA binding instead reveals TR2i unexpectedly induces a unique ATP-RAD51 dimer conformation that accommodates nucleation onto double-stranded B-DNA unsuited for HDR initiation. Structural, biochemical, and molecular results with interface-guided mutations uncover TR2i’s FP mechanism. Proline-driven secondary structure stabilizes residue triads and spans the RAD51 dimer, engaging pivotal interactions of RAD51 M210 and BRCA2 S3291/P3292, the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation site that toggles between FP during S phase and HDR in G2. TR2i evidently acts as an allosteric clamp, switching RAD51 from ssDNA to double-stranded and B-DNA binding, enforcing FP over HDR, challenging the current BRCA2-RAD51 dogma.

Cette étude a pour objectif de décrire, d’un point de vue linguistique et sociologique, l’implication de spécialistes en médecine générale auprès des patients (apparentés à risque élevé de cancer colorectal ou patients index) et leur posture communicationnelle dans le cadre du dépistage familial auprès des différents protagonistes (autres médecins, patients index, apparentés). Méthode : Elle s’appuie sur 29 entretiens semi-directifs avec des spécialistes en médecine générale français de patients index et/ou de leurs apparentés réalisés par téléphone. records.title: A Comprehensive Review on Thyroid Management And Therapeutic Potential of Medicinal Plants
records.abstract: Thyroid diseases are widespread endocrine disorders that affect a significant portion of the global population. The pathology associated with specific types or stages of thyroid disease is complex and intricately linked to various biological functions. While the mortality rate associated with thyroid dysfunction is relatively low, it can lead to metabolic and immunological disorders that result in considerable discomfort for affected individuals. Currently, numerous pharmaceutical options are available for managing thyroid disease; however, issues such as drug toxicity and prolonged treatment durations highlight the urgent need for more effective alternatives. Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent endocrine conditions worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and contributing significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Effective thyroid management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and long-term monitoring to prevent complications and optimize patient outcomes.

records.title: Water Lily or Camelotte Sign in Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst – An Orphan Disease
records.abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

records.title: Caracterización clínica y epidemiológica de la bronquitis aguda en pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años durante 2023
records.abstract: Introducción: La bronquitis aguda es una de las infecciones respiratorias más frecuentes en la población pediátrica y representa una causa importante de consulta y hospitalización en América Latina. Metodología: Se realizó un estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo mediante revisión de historias clínicas electrónicas de 83 pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años con diagnóstico de bronquitis aguda atendidos durante enero–diciembre de 2023. Resultados: Predominó el sexo masculino (61,4%) y el grupo de 2 a 4 años (44,6%). La tos fue la manifestación más frecuente (92,8%), seguida de fiebre (62,7%) y sibilancias (51,8%). Las complicaciones más frecuentes fueron la exacerbación del asma (10,8%) y la otitis media aguda (8,4%). Los broncodilatadores inhalados fueron el tratamiento más utilizado (75,9%), seguidos de antipiréticos (72,3%); los antibióticos se emplearon en 13,3%. Conclusiones: La bronquitis aguda presentó predominio masculino, mayor frecuencia en niños de 2 a 4 años y una presentación clínica caracterizada principalmente por tos. Las complicaciones graves fueron poco frecuentes y el uso de antibióticos fue limitado.

affiliations: School of Medicine, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA.
records.abstract: Background Positive paediatric cancer treatment outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) significantly lag behind those in high-income countries. One reason for this disparity is high treatment abandonment rates in LMICs, defined as a failure to start or complete curative-intent therapy after a cancer diagnosis. We did a systematic review and meta-analysis to describe interventions aimed at reducing treatment abandonment in paediatric patients with cancer in LMICs. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we completed a comprehensive search of MEDLINE Ovid, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane on Oct 21, 2022, with an updated search on Oct 21, 2025. Studies were included if they met the following criteria: studied an intervention on treatment abandonment; included patients with cancer aged 18 years and younger; were conducted in LMICs as defined by the World Bank income classification; contained quantification of treatment abandonment by patients in a comparison and intervention group; and had a full-text article available. We restricted inclusion to English-language studies. We systematically assessed the quality of the studies and conducted a random-effects meta-analysis of risk ratios. Findings Among the 2263 articles identified across the two searches, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. affiliations: Cancer Epidemiology Research Program, Catalan Institute of Oncology, Bellvitge Biomedical Research Institute (IDIBELL), L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, Spain; Centro de Investigación Biomédica en Red de Epidemiología y Salud Pública (CIBERESP CB06/02/0073), Madrid, Spain; Programa de Doctorat en Medicina i Recerca Translacional, Universitat de Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain.
records.abstract: Background Regularly updated global estimates are needed to monitor progress in cervical cancer screening, a key pillar of WHO's strategy to eliminate cervical cancer. We aimed to update estimates of cervical cancer screening coverage in 194 WHO member states and eight associated countries and territories for 2022, including the first global assessment of human papillomavirus (HPV) test-based screening adoption and roll-out. Methods In this review and synthetic analysis, we used an established method to estimate standardised cervical cancer screening coverage in 2022. We used programme and population-based coverage data collected up to Jan 31, 2024, selecting the sources considered most representative of each country or territory's screening situation in 2022. Preliminary estimates were reviewed through a WHO country consultation (April-May, 2024; with additional responses received until July 2025). HPV testing coverage was estimated based on HPV test-based screening implementation levels, by country and year. Estimates were applied to 2022 populations and aggregated by region and country-income level. Findings Cervical cancer screening recommendations were identified in 161 (80%) of 202 countries, with 92 (57%) of 161 countries recommending HPV test-based screening. records.title: Perineal Urethrostomy After Urethral Stricture: Step-by-Step Surgical Technique.
affiliations: Serviço de Urologia, Hospital Federal da Lagoa, Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brasil.
records.abstract: PURPOSE: Urethral stricture is a chronic narrowing of the urethral lumen caused by inflammation and iatrogenic interventions, including previous surgery and prostate cancer treatment (1). Treatment options include urethral dilation, internal urethrotomy, urethroplasty, and perineal urethrostomy. Perineal urethrostomy creates a permanent urethral meatus and is increasingly considered a primary treatment option for complex cases or patients with significant comorbidities (2, 3). It is associated with high patient satisfaction, preserved continence, and favorable voiding outcomes (4). This video presents a systematic, step-by-step description of the surgical technique. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 73-year-old man with complex, recurrent urethral stricture had undergone multiple reconstructive and endoscopic procedures before perineal urethrostomy in February 2026. His medical history was notable for Bowen's disease of the glans penis. Under spinal anesthesia, with the patient in the high lithotomy position, an inverted U-shaped perineal incision was made, and the bulbocavernosus muscle was dissected to expose the bulbar urethra. The perineal skin was sutured to the opened urethra, incorporating the urethral mucosal edge, corpus spongiosum adventitia, and skin edge. The dorsal urethral plate was left intact, preserving longitudinal blood flow within the corpus spongiosum. A Foley catheter was inserted through the proximal urethrotomy into the bladder. Without the adenoma, the capsule is flaccid and offers no counter-resistance; without haptic feedback, the planes of the bladder neck (6) and neurovascular bundle (7) become indistinct. records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite recent advances in pediatric oncology, 15% of children and adolescents with cancer in Germany (approx. 350 per year) die of their disease. Even when the unfavorable prognosis is clear early on, patients often do not receive palliative care until shortly before death when the symptom burden is high. This causes unnecessary distress for everyone involved. METHODS: Systematic searches for pertinent guidelines and scientific publications up to 2023/2024 were carried out in accordance with the AWMF specifications for S3-level clinical practice guidelines. Of the 17 821 primary publications screened (databases: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane), 66 were used as sources of evidence for the guideline recommendations. Individual recommendations from three adult guidelines were also adopted after appropriate adjustment for the special situation and needs of children and adolescents. records.abstract: PURPOSE: This study presents a structured narrative review of lower urinary tract (LUT) complications following prostate cancer (PCa) radiotherapy and proposes an organ-based clinical framework for their evaluation and management. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, including studies published between January 2000 and December 2025 and supplemented by seminal studies in radiation biology and reconstructive urology. Search terms included prostate cancer, radiotherapy, radiation cystitis, bladder dysfunction, urethral stricture, bladder neck contracture, urinary incontinence, urinary fistulae, ureteral stricture, and post-radiotherapy outlet surgery. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively and organized into organ-specific domains. RESULTS: Radiation-induced LUT complications include radiation cystitis, detrusor overactivity and impaired compliance associated with bladder fibrosis, urethral and bladder neck strictures, sphincteric insufficiency with urinary incontinence, urinary fistulae, and ureteral strictures. These conditions frequently coexist because of the multifocal and progressive nature of radiation injury. records.title: Multiphoton Imaging of the Tibial Bone Marrow for In Vivo Spatial-Temporal Analysis of Myeloma Microenvironment and Treatment.
affiliations: Department of Pathology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx, NY, USA. david.fooksman@einsteinmed.edu.
records.abstract: The bone marrow is a critical niche for multiple myeloma initiation, growth, and pathology. The biological and technical complexities of the bone marrow microenvironment make it challenging to study tumor physiology in situ. We have developed a thinned-bone surgical preparation for imaging the mouse tibial bone marrow. Using this approach, we have studied the spatial organization and temporal dynamics of myeloma cells, their interactions with the immune microenvironment, and the effects of acute drug treatments. In this chapter, we detail a protocol describing this procedure and present two use cases for intravital imaging to study dynamics tumors. In one study, we describe the use of photoactivation to capture live immune cells that are present within myeloma foci within the bone marrow for downstream analysis by flow cytometry or by other methods. In the second use case, we used imaging to capture effects of drug treatment in real-time in situ in the bone marrow to understand mechanisms of action and side effects.

records.title: Measurable Residual Disease.
affiliations: Department of Hematopathology, ACTREC, Tata Memorial Center, HBNI University, Room 18, CCE Building, ACTREC, Sector 22, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, 410210, India. docprt@gmail.com.
records.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) serves as a critical biomarker of prognosis, treatment efficacy, and clinical outcome. It captures the presence of residual tumor cells below the detection threshold of conventional microscopy. Multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC) offers a rapid, cost-efficient, and widely applicable platform for MRD detection through leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIPs) and deviation-from-normal (DfN) antigen maturation patterns. This technique underpins a wide range of clinical applications, including risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and post-transplant surveillance. This chapter outlines essential technical parameters for achieving high-sensitivity MRD detection across hematologic malignancies such as B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, MM, and CLL. Key topics covered include material required, reagent preparation, antibody panel design, sample processing and acquisition, gating strategies, and illustrative examples. Special emphasis is given to adaptations necessary for MRD monitoring following CD19-targeted therapies in B-ALL. By integrating rigorous methodology with evolving innovations, MFC continues to advance as a precise and expedient tool for MRD assessment, contributing significantly to personalized treatment strategies.

records.abstract: Flow cytometry has made it possible to identify human B cell subsets based on surface and intracellular antigens, a process known as immunophenotyping. CD19 and CD20 are commonly expressed in all B cells; the presence or absence of CD27 separates memory B cells from naïve cells, while IgD and IgM are used to distinguish naïve from transitional B cells. Markers such as CD38, CD27, and CD24 are helpful to identify plasmablasts and immature B cells. CD21 points to mature B cells, CD10 is on immature B cells, CD138 marks plasma cells, and CD5 is high in regulatory B cells. Memory B cells have less CD23 than naïve B cells. B cells are multifaceted. They present antigens (APCs), secrete antibodies, and keep the immune system in check. Identifying B-cell subsets in clinical settings-especially for diagnosing immune disorders, autoimmune diseases, and blood cancers like leukemias and lymphomas. Knowing which B cells are present in a certain disease setting helps clinicians understand how far a disease has progressed and how active it is. With this information, a treatment that fits the patient's needs can be selected, ones that target B cells directly, like anti-CD20 antibodies. With flow cytometry as a tool, we can spot B-cell malignancies like chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), follicular lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, and multiple myeloma. records.abstract: We are conducting a scoping review focusing on the topic of "family accommodation", defined as “actions that family members engage in, or deliberately do not engage in, to help alleviate or avoid a child’s distress” in parents of children, adolescents and young adults (CAYA) with a cancer diagnosis. The scoping review aims to explore: 1) How does parental accommodation impact the health, health-related behaviours, and mental health of CAYA with a cancer diagnosis; 2) how does parental accommodation impact the emotional and psychological well-being of parents in families with CAYA with a cancer diagnosis; and 3) how is family accommodation in the context of cancer being measured.

records.title: Majority Filter For Enhancing Pixel-Based Random Forest Land Cover Classification In Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency
records.abstract: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noise, which undermines map reliability. This study aimed to integrate Random Forest (RF) classification and majority filtering to enhance the quality of land cover mapping in Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency. RF was applied to Sentinel-2 image data with varying numbers of trees (ntree) to determine the optimal model performance. Subsequently, majority filtering was applied to each classification result to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence. The evaluation employed multiple accuracy metrics, including User’s Accuracy (UA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), F1-Score, Overall Accuracy (OA), and Kappa Coefficient (KC). Comprehensive accuracy increased with the ntree until reaching an optimal point. Beyond this point, additional ntree resulted in diminishing returns. Applying majority filtering as a post-processing procedure led to further improvements in classification accuracy. While majority filtering can reduce classification noise and improve the visual quality of land cover maps, it also carries the risk of removing small, accurately classified land cover patches. records.title: Tumor-treating fields in gastrointestinal cancers: Mechanisms, clinical evidence, and emerging precision therapy
records.abstract: Tumor-treating fields (TTFields) are low-intensity, intermediate-frequency alternating electric fields that convert physical energy into biological stress within dividing cancer cells. Initially recognized for their ability to disrupt mitosis, TTFields are now understood to influence a broader range of cancer-related processes, including DNA replication, repair pathways, cellular organization, and immunogenic cell death. These mechanisms are particularly relevant to gastrointestinal malignancies, where deep anatomy, stromal barriers, organ motion, peritoneal dissemination, and cumulative systemic toxicity limit conventional treatment escalation. Pancreatic cancer is currently the leading gastrointestinal indication for TTFields. In the PANOVA-3 trial, TTFields combined with standard chemotherapy improved overall survival without additional systemic toxicity, although tumor shrinkage and conventional progression-free survival remained unchanged. Evidence in hepatocellular, gastric, biliary tract, and colorectal cancers remains preliminary and should be interpreted as mechanistic or hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing. This article argues that TTFields should not be understood as a simple on-or-off device exposure. records.title: Metabolic commonalities in colorectal and gastric cancer: Taurine metabolism as a key regulatory node and its translational implications
affiliations: Dongzhimen Hospital Affiliated to Beijing University of Chinese Medicine
records.abstract: As the two most frequently occurring digestive system cancers, colorectal cancer and gastric cancer share many commonalities in terms of their epidemiology, metabolic reprogramming and microenvironmental regulation. Recent studies have demonstrated that dysregulated taurine metabolism is an important hub in the metabolic network of both cancers, contributing to tumor progression via several mechanisms, including modulation of energy metabolism, remodeling of the immune microenvironment, interaction with gut microbiota, and maintenance of oxidative stress balance. The aberrant features of taurine metabolism and the molecular mechanisms in colorectal cancer and gastric cancer were systematically discussed, the central role of taurine metabolism in tumor metabolic reprogramming, immune evasion and inflammation-cancer transformation was discussed in detail, and the clinical translational prospects of targeting taurine metabolism as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target were outlined, which provides new theoretical foundations and strategic insights for the precise prevention and treatment of both cancers.

records.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in gastrointestinal malignancies: Friend or foe?
records.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), chromatin-based webs released by activated neutrophils, were first described as antimicrobial scaffolds, but these structures now appear in sterile inflammation, thrombosis, and cancer. In gastrointestinal malignancies, experimental and clinical studies have connected NETs with tumor growth, immune escape, cancer-associated thrombosis, postoperative recurrence, and metastatic spread. NET-derived DNA, histones, neutrophil elastase, myeloperoxidase, and citrullinated histones can remodel the tumor microenvironment, shield tumor cells from cytotoxic lymphocytes, promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, awaken dormant cells, and help metastatic cells colonize distant organs. However, NETs are not simply harmful. They remain part of host defense and may restrain tumor cells in selected inflammatory, infectious, or treatment-related settings. This review summarizes NET biology in colorectal, gastric, hepatocellular, pancreatic, and other gastrointestinal cancers, focusing on the therapies that inhibit NET formation, degrade NET scaffolds, or block NET-tumor cell interactions.

records.abstract: BACKGROUND Metachronous liver metastasis (MLM) represents a major contributor to disease relapse and poor survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). The prognostic value of combining intra- and peritumoral radiomics features for predicting MLM has not been fully explored. AIM To develop and validate a computed tomography-based intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics model for predicting MLM and a nomogram for predicting 5-year liver metastasis-free survival (LMFS) of CRC patients. METHODS This retrospective study included CRC patients who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography. records.title: Extracellular vesicles in gastrointestinal diseases: A narrative minireview of translational readiness
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate communication among epithelial, immune, stromal, microbial, and tumor compartments in gastrointestinal diseases. This narrative minireview integrates inflammatory bowel disease and major gastrointestinal malignancies (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and liver cancers) using a five-stage translational-readiness framework: Discovery, analytical validation, clinical validation, regulatory development, and implementation. We distinguish discovery-stage and preclinical findings from clinically validated applications. EV cargo and engineered EV platforms show potential for biomarker panels, liquid biopsy, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine, but no broad EV assay or therapeutic platform is established for routine precision gastroenterology. Key barriers include pre-analytical variability, isolation-dependent results, incomplete cargo attribution, cohort heterogeneity, limited independent validation, and manufacturing and safety requirements. Progress will require standardized workflows, disease-specific comparators, prospective multicenter validation, and evidence-calibrated integration of EV data with conventional biomarkers and multi-omics.

records.title: Helicobacter pylori status in gastric cancer immunotherapy: Conflicting clinical associations, immune-microbial mechanisms, and biomarker challenges
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important treatment option for gastric cancer, but therapeutic responses remain highly heterogeneous. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ), a major risk factor for gastric carcinogenesis, may continue to influence tumor immunity and immunotherapy outcomes after cancer develops. However, current clinical findings are inconsistent, and the biomarker value of H. pylori remains uncertain. This review critically summarizes the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking H. pylori status to ICI outcomes in gastric cancer. Potential mechanisms include regulation of programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 signaling, T-cell function, antigen presentation, myeloid immunosuppression, and microbial ecology. The divergent clinical results may reflect differences in infection status, detection methods, tumor molecular subtypes, disease stage, treatment setting, and previous therapeutic exposures. Current evidence does not support H. pylori as a validated predictive biomarker for ICI response. Rather, it may represent a context-dependent indicator of the tumor-immune-microbial background. Prospective longitudinal studies with standardized definitions of current active infection, previous infection of uncertain current status, successfully eradicated infection, and no evidence of previous infection are needed to determine whether specific H. pylori -related biological states modify the relative benefit of immunotherapy.

records.abstract: The epidemiology of gastric cancer is changing in Western populations. records.title: Breast cancer screening in Europe and the role of general practitioners: A 32-country comparative survey.
records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is the commonest cancer in women, and screening can allow earlier-stage diagnosis. While there are European recommendations on the age-range and frequency of breast cancer screening, participation in these programmes varies substantially, and this could be due to differences in how they are organised and implemented. The role that primary healthcare professionals play in the process is unclear.We aimed to describe the breast cancer screening programmes in European countries and investigate how primary healthcare professionals are involved in this screening process.Methods A cross-sectional survey in 32 countries. Key informants with relevant expertise answered online questions about the characteristics of their screening programmes and general practitioners' (GPs') roles in this. Responses were refined through an iterative consensus process. Data were examined to identify patterns in GP engagement.Results We found important differences between European breast cancer screening systems. While most had population-based screening, four countries relied on opportunistic screening. In 15 countries GPs had little or no involvement in the process of breast cancer screening, and in 13 countries GPs had some involvement, including identifying eligible patients, issuing referrals, and following-up results. Screening uptake rates tended to be higher in countries with well-established population-based screening programmes which give little or no GP involvement.

affiliations: University of West Bohemia in Pilsen
records.journal: ASEAN Journal for Science and Engineering in Materials
records.abstract: This review evaluates the application of deep learning (DL) for the predictive modeling of electronic materials in computer engineering. We analyzed peer-reviewed literature across four major databases, focusing exclusively on advanced architectures like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative models. Results indicate these models accurately predict critical properties, such as band gaps and thermal conductivity, for next-generation semiconductors, 2D materials, and memristors. These high accuracies are achieved because architectures like GNNs effectively capture complex 3D spatial interactions without requiring manual feature engineering. However, practical fabrication remains hindered by data scarcity, algorithmic opacity, and a profound "Sim-to-Real Gap". While DL accelerates predictive design, sustaining Moore's Law ultimately requires developing autonomous "Self-Driving Labs" and Large Material Models to bridge digital predictions with physical synthesis.

records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: AIMS: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems. However, its prognostic impact in stages II and III colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inconsistently defined. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prognostic value of high-grade TB in stage II-III CRC. Subgroup analysis stratified by TNM stage revealed that high-grade TB consistently predicted adverse outcomes in both stage II and stage III disease. CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms that high-grade TB is an independent prognostic factor in stage II-III CRC, consistently associated with worse DFS, OS and CSS. records.abstract: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer formed by glycoproteins, glycolipids, proteoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans at the outer cell surface. These changes affect how tumor cells sense force, bind the extracellular matrix, cluster receptors, evade immune surveillance, survive in circulation, and arrest at distant vascular beds. records.title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review.
records.abstract: Shoulder pain is a major cause of work absenteeism, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Although nonsurgical treatments like physical therapy are recommended as the first line of management, 40% of patients are referred for surgery before exploring these options. This review aimed to identify existing triage models used for shoulder pain referrals for surgery, guidelines for shoulder pain management that include criteria for surgical referral, and indications for surgery. An integrative review approach was used to comprehensively search major databases (Medline, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL Plus) and gray literature. Articles on triage models, referral processes, or surgery candidacy for shoulder pain were included. The searches retrieved 4510 articles, with 480 selected for full review and 71 articles included in this synthesis. Thirty-seven articles described various triage models and clinical decision-making processes for managing shoulder pain, including determining when to refer for surgical consultation and the indications for surgery. Seventeen articles compared surgical and nonsurgical treatments to identify surgical indicators, 10 articles examined factors affecting decision-making, and 7 articles explored predictor models for surgical outcomes. The findings underscore the need for a multifactorial decision-making process that acknowledges the complexity of pain within a biopsychosocial framework and incorporates patients' personal preferences into the triage decision-making process.

Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. affiliations: Beijing Institute of Microbiology and Epidemiology
records.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

records.journal: CSUSB ScholarWorks (California State University, San Bernardino)
records.abstract: Neural crest cells (NCCs) are a transient, highly migratory embryonic stem cell population unique to vertebrates. During development, they give rise to diverse tissues, including craniofacial cartilage, peripheral neurons, glia, melanocytes, and components of the cardiac outflow tract. As NCCs migrate through complex environments, precise spatial and temporal regulation of gene expression is needed to coordinate migration and developmental fate. Defects in NCC development and migration can result in a broad class of disorders known as neurocristopathies (NCPs), including craniofacial abnormalities, Hirschsprung’s disease, and neuroblastoma. Despite the importance of NCC migration during development, many of the molecular mechanisms regulating this process are still not fully understood. One mechanism that enables spatial regulation of gene expression is RNA localization, the transport of messenger RNAs (mRNAs) to specific subcellular regions. Interestingly, in these systems, disruption of mRNA localization alone is enough to reduce migratory efficiency, suggesting that RNA localization itself plays an important role in regulating migration. records.abstract: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH), including neighborhood conditions, structural racism, and socioeconomic disadvantage, contribute to disease development and progression. Epigenetic mechanisms may provide a biological pathway linking adverse social conditions to chronic disease disparities. This dissertation examined the influence of SDOH on SLE disparities through evidence synthesis and empirical investigation to inform public health practice and policy. Methods: This integrated learning experience consisted of three complementary manuscripts. Aim 1 was a PRISMA-ScR scoping review examining associations among SDOH, epigenetic mechanisms, and chronic disease outcomes. Aim 2 was a secondary cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from a case-control study the Social Factors, Epigenomics, and Lupus in African American Women (SELA) Study examining neighborhood racial composition and SLE disease activity using generalized estimating equations (GEE). records.title: Exploring Micronutrient Intake, Ultra-Processed Food Consumption, and Their Associations With Metabolic Syndrome and Food-Related Behaviors Among Adolescents in the United States
records.abstract: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth and development during which good nutrition is especially important for long-term health. However, many adolescents in the United States consume large amounts of ultra-processed foods, including packaged snacks, sugary drinks, and fast food. This dissertation used nationally representative data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017–2020 to examine micronutrient intake, ultra-processed food consumption, food-related behaviors, and metabolic health among U.S. adolescents. The first part of the study examined usual nutrient intake and micronutrient adequacy. Overall micronutrient adequacy was high at 96%. However, important dietary concerns remained. Many adolescents had low intakes of calcium and magnesium and consumed high amounts of saturated fat, added sugars, and sodium. Adolescents who used dietary supplements had higher intakes of several vitamins and minerals, but supplement use did not eliminate all nutrient shortfalls. Ultra-processed foods contributed about two-thirds of total daily energy intake, with differences observed across demographic groups. The second part examined whether food-related behaviors were associated with ultra-processed food consumption and micronutrient adequacy. records.title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
records.abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era. This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer therapies, rather than summarizing therapeutic efficacy. The evidence shows a persistent mismatch between contemporary toxicity phenotypes and existing trial design: Most studies continue to focus on anthracycline-associated left ventricular dysfunction and surrogate imaging endpoints, while immune-mediated myocarditis, cytokine release syndrome-related cardiomyopathy, vascular toxicities, arrhythmias, and other emerging phenotypes remain inadequately represented, compounded by limited biological stratification, one-size-fits-all prevention strategies, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and insufficient mechanism-specific monitoring. Progress in cardio-oncology prevention is constrained not only by the availability of candidate cardioprotective interventions but by the near-uniform persistence of a single trial architecture across mechanistically distinct toxicities. records.title: [Advances in precision management of aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia in breast cancer].
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
records.abstract: Endocrine therapy is a core strategy throughout the management of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, substantially reducing the risks of recurrence and death. However, treatment-related adverse events, particularly aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia (AIA), have become a major barrier to treatment adherence. Current evidence suggests that AIA cannot be explained solely by estrogen deprivation. T-cell leukemia/lymphoma 1A (TCL1A) genetic variants, interleukin-17/nuclear factor-κB-related inflammatory pathways, and an imbalance between T helper 17 and regulatory T cells may jointly contribute to its development, suggesting that AIA may represent a modifiable pathological process. Accordingly, its management should shift from symptom-oriented palliation toward a precise supportive-care model integrating risk stratification, early intervention, and long-term adherence maintenance. From a translational medicine perspective, this review synthesizes evidence on the pathogenesis of AIA, intervention trials, and the latest guidelines, and proposes a three-stage AIA management framework adapted to Chinese clinical practice (baseline assessment and prevention-stratified intervention-digital closed-loop follow-up). The framework emphasizes the importance of alleviating adverse events to maintain treatment adherence and improve long-term outcomes but requires prospective clinical validation.

records.title: Advanced three-dimensional bioprinting for in vitro tumor model engineering: From biomimetic model construction to personalized precision medicine
records.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting technology offers a transformative approach for constructing biomimetic tumor organoid models that overcome the limitations of traditional two-dimensional cell cultures and animal models. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in 3D bioprinted tumor organoids, emphasizing extrusion-based, inkjet-based, and lithography-based bioprinting methods. These technologies enable precise spatial control of cell distribution and tissue architecture, achieving high reproducibility while maintaining complex tumor microenvironmental characteristics. Applications across multiple cancer types—including colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, breast, glioma, renal, bladder, lung, and thyroid cancers—demonstrate significant potential for drug screening, tumor heterogeneity research, and preclinical evaluation of individualized treatment responses. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain regarding multicellular complexity simulation, technical resolution, and biomaterial optimization. Future directions include integrating four-dimensional bioprinting, multiomics analysis, and immune microenvironment reconstruction to enhance physiological fidelity and clinical applicability, ultimately advancing precision oncology and personalized cancer treatment strategies.

records.abstract: Abstract Melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer requiring early detection, yet automated analysis remains affected by lesion variation, calibration errors, uncertainty, and subgroup disparities. This study presents MelanoFusion, a hybrid framework integrating explainability, uncertainty estimation, and fairness-oriented representation learning for melanoma detection. It combines EfficientNetV2-S and Swin Transformer encoders with cross-attention, lesion attention, feature-pyramid processing, multi-scale transformer layers, and an uncertainty head. Images were resized to 224 × 224 and processed using hair removal, median filtering, contrast enhancement, colour normalization, and watershed-based lesion priors; U-Net was used for lesion segmentation. MelanoFusion was evaluated against DenseNet121, ResNet101, EfficientNetV2-S, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and Swin Transformer on HAM10000, ISIC 2018, and PH². Calibration was favourable on HAM10000, with an expected calibration error of 0.116. records.title: Primate-specific SSX1 is required for CPSF6-dependent spermatocyte transcription and human fertility
affiliations: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China
First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University
records.abstract: Abstract Genetic variation is a major cause of male infertility, and defining the underlying mechanisms is essential for developing effective interventions. SSX1 is a primate specific gene whose deficiency has been linked to sperm malformations in humans and cynomolgus monkeys, yet its pathogenic mechanism remains unclear. Here, by whole exome sequencing of a cohort of 536 men with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (OAT), we identified three previously unreported SSX1 variants, including two deletion alleles and one selective splice site variant. SSX1 deficiency was associated with a characteristic OAT phenotype featuring short, coiled flagella and severe loss of the central pair microtubules. SSX1 is expressed in early spermatocytes, and its loss disrupted the expression of spermiogenesis and sperm function related genes that are transcribed in advance during the spermatocyte stage. Mechanistically, SSX1 acts as a transcriptional regulator by interacting with the transcription and processing factor CPSF6 and promoting nuclear recruitment of the CPSF complex, with functional relevance in both spermatocytes and spermatids. Collectively, our study supports a functional role for SSX1 with CPSF6 in human spermatogenesis, expands the genetic diagnostic spectrum of OAT, and provides a transcription focused framework for precision management of male infertility.

records.abstract: Abstract Background Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) lacks reliable molecular biomarkers for early detection and classification. While pathway-based prognostic models have been reported, the role of organelle dysfunction, particularly Golgi biology, remains uninvestigated. records.abstract: Liver disease remains a major health concern globally, especially in the Asia-Pacific region, yet many low-income countries lack robust registries to track and manage it effectively. This systematic review analyzed 139 publications covering 62 liver disease registries to assess their structure, data management, quality monitoring, and sustainability, with the goal of informing registry development in low-resource settings like the Philippines. Most registries (72.6%) focused on a single disease, primarily viral hepatitis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and were commonly found in high-income countries. National-level implementation was typical (50%), though only a third had clear governance structures, and nearly half lacked long-term funding. While half employed quality monitoring, data security measures were often unspecified. The findings underscore the vital role of liver disease registries in improving care and informing policy, while highlighting persistent gaps in governance, standardization, and sustainability.

records.title: Multiplexed FRET-FLIM profiling of immune checkpoint interactions predicts response to atezolizumab in urothelial carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have shown great promise in treating bladder cancer and are now part of the standard treatment for advanced disease. However, many patients still fail to respond to treatment, and at present, many biomarkers are assessed but have yet shown only limited results. Therefore, with the advent of combination treatments and the increase in immune-related adverse event, the search for reliable predictive biomarkers is paramount. Using a multiplexed enhanced FRET-FLIM-based technique (QF-Pro), we quantified the interaction of PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4/CD80, and TIGIT/CD155 immune checkpoints in a pre-treatment TMA of 46 patients treated with atezolizumab. The association between higher PD-1/PD-L1 ICP interaction state and treatment efficacy was demonstrated in the male sample cohort, where it identified patients with better progression-free survival. Conversely, patients exhibiting higher CTLA-4/CD80 engagement had a worse response to atezolizumab. Remarkably, the dual assessment of patients with high PD-1/PD-L1 and low CTLA-4/CD80 allowed to identify the best responders. These results indicate that the monitoring of patients’ immune profile in urothelial carcinoma might be critical in identifying patients who may benefit from combination therapy.

records.title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology
records.abstract: R-2-Hydroxyglutarate (R2HG), an oncometabolite predominantly produced by mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1/2 (IDH1/2) in various cancers, is known to drive cancer progression through noncovalent inhibition of α-ketoglutarate (αKG)-dependent enzymes. In this work, we propose an alternative mechanism wherein R2HG contributes to cancer development via covalent modification of biologically critical lysines, a process termed lysine-R2HGylation (KR2HG). We designed and synthesized R2HG-mimicking probes and demonstrated their effectiveness in facilitating KR2HG target profiling and site mapping. We identified KR2HG as a post-translational modification, confirmed its C5-linkage on GSTP1(K209), and demonstrated that SIRT5 functions as a deacylase for GSTP1-KR2HG in vitro. Furthermore, we found that R2HG slightly but significantly inhibits the enzymatic activity of GSTP1 through KR2HG and dramatically suppresses monocyte differentiation via this catalytically important lysine modification. Our findings provide an alternative perspective on the role of R2HG in leukemia progression and offer a practical tool for the clinical investigation of R2HG-elevated cancers. R-2-hydroxyglutarate is a cancer-linked metabolite whose mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, the authors identify and structurally characterize lysineR2HGylation as a protein modification and develop probes that reveal GSTP1 as a functional target in leukemia cells.

records.title: The AKAP1 ribonucleoprotein network integrates mitochondrial homeostasis, P-body dynamics and protein translation in cycling cells
affiliations: Istituto per il Sistema Produzione Animale in Ambiente Mediterraneo
records.abstract: Abstract Integration of protein translation and mitochondrial activities represents a mechanism to rapidly adapt anabolic processes to specific cellular needs. This aspect is of particular importance for cell division when mitochondrial dynamics, oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis are timely coordinated to allow a faithful completion of the cell cycle. However, the mechanisms coupling mitochondrial homeostasis to protein translation in cycling cells are largely unknown. Here, we report the identification of a molecular network assembled by AKAP1 at mitochondria that includes mRNA, components of the translation repression machinery (P-bodies) and mitotic kinases (CDK1/2). During interphase, the AKAP1 complex dynamically coordinates cAMP signaling, mitochondrial activity, P-body dynamics and protein translation to ensure proper cell cycle progression. At mitosis, CDK-induced proteolysis of AKAP1 via a cullin-mediated ubiquitin pathway reduces oxidative metabolism, promotes mitochondrial fission and reshapes mRNA translation, finalizing the cell cycle. Disruption of this network impairs cell cycle progression. These findings unveil a regulatory mechanism controlled by AKAP1 that functionally and dynamically links oxidative metabolism to protein synthesis in cycling cells. Targeting this biological node could help to restore deranged mitochondrial function during degenerative and proliferative disorders.

records.title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
affiliations: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
records.abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

records.title: Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones: distinctive fungal polyketide alkaloid hybrids with intriguing therapeutic applications: a comprehensive update
records.abstract: Covering: 2005-2025Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones are a fascinating class of fungal natural products that possess an intricate chemical structure characterized by a distinctive macrocyclic ring fused to a decahydrofluorene core. Known for their complex architectures as PKS-NRPS hybrids, these metabolites are isolated from various fungi and have attracted significant attention due to their potent pharmacological properties, including antimicrobial, antifungal, and anticancer effects. This review article aims to shed light on the structural diversities of 52 fungal-derived pyrrocidines and hirsutellones reported over the period of 2005-2025, providing insights into their chemistry, biosynthetic origins, pharmacokinetic profiles, and structure-activity relationships (SARs). Furthermore, we critically evaluate their promising therapeutic potential, highlighting the opportunities they present for modern drug discovery and development.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Imaging Biomarkers for Distinguishing Pseudoprogression from True Progression after Cellular Immunotherapy in Glioblastoma
records.abstract: Abstract Pseudoprogression, transient radiographic worsening caused by treatment-related inflammation rather than tumor growth, is a well-recognized pitfall after chemoradiotherapy for glioblastoma and is becoming more relevant as checkpoint inhibitors and cellular immunotherapies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells enter clinical testing. Conventional structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cannot reliably separate pseudoprogression from true progression, exposing patients to premature treatment discontinuation or unnecessary intensification. Quantitative, artificial-intelligence-based imaging analysis (radiomics, and its molecular extension radiogenomics) is an emerging candidate solution. In this narrative review we synthesize the evidence on radiomics and radiogenomics for differentiating pseudoprogression from true progression in glioblastoma, with emphasis on the immunotherapy and cellular-therapy context. records.title: 3D ultrasound shear wave elastography quantifies myocardial stiffness and anisotropy in the human heart
affiliations: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
records.abstract: Abstract Myocardial stiffness (MS) is a key property of diastolic cardiac function which is altered in various cardiomyopathies. Its quantitative evaluation remains challenging due to the myocardium’s complex anisotropic fibers architecture and dynamic contraction. We developed a novel 3D shear wave elastography (3D-SWE) system suitable for clinical translation based on 3D ultrafast volumetric imaging for the quantitative assessment of MS in the human heart. Validation was performed on calibrated phantoms and ex vivo in porcine hearts compared to standard 2D-SWE. In vivo feasibility was demonstrated on healthy volunteers and patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (CA). We demonstrated that 3D shear wave propagation can be observed in vivo and that 3D-SWE provides quantitative assessment of myocardium anisotropy through shear wave velocities along and across fibers and fractional anisotropy. In addition, MS was significantly elevated in CA patients compared to normal myocardium, whereas the fractional anisotropy was decreased. The feasibility of volumetric MS mapping on the human heart was demonstrated showing the potential of 3D-SWE as a clinically oriented tool for early diagnosis of cardiomyopathies such as CA.

records.abstract: Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably between individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. records.title: The impact of epigenetic chemical probes: expanding targeting modalities and disease understanding
records.abstract: Small-molecule chemical modulators (chemical probes) targeting epigenetic regulators are essential tools for research by enabling precise temporal control over chromatin dynamics. Over the past two decades, large international efforts have produced hundreds of validated and openly accessible chemical probes. While the field was initially driven by occupancy-based catalytic inhibitors, there has been a recent shift toward context-dependent target engagement and induced proximity strategies. By repurposing established chemical ligands, next-generation heterobifunctional modalities (e.g., PROTACs and RIPTACs) can drive targeted protein degradation or disrupt multi-protein complexes to achieve deeper functional effects. In the present review, we discuss the evolution of epigenetic chemical probes, the emergence of induced proximity strategies, and the importance of recognizing that different targeting modalities for a given protein may yield distinct biological outcomes. Collectively, the history of epigenetic probes provides a foundation for Target 2035, an international initiative led by the Structural Genomics Consortium aimed at developing pharmacological modulators across the human proteome.

Initially identified as a key regulator of copper ion homeostasis, accumulating evidence has shown that COMMD1 does not function as a canonical tumour suppressor or oncogene in malignant tumours. Instead, it serves as a context‑dependent molecular hub whose activity is dynamically influenced by cellular background, signalling pathway status and post‑translational modifications. On the one hand, COMMD1 exerts antitumour effects by inhibiting NF‑κB and hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1 signalling, regulating DNA damage repair, modulating cell cycle progression and enhancing apoptotic sensitivity. records.abstract: Abstract Proteomic analysis of blood plasma is a promising tool for cancer screening. A method for screening a panel of 100 clinically significant plasma proteins using targeted mass spectrometry based on multiple reaction monitoring (MRM MS) was developed. Quantitative MRM MS analysis of plasma samples from healthy donors (N = 52) and patients with hematologic malignancies, multiple myeloma (MM; N = 35) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DL; N = 30), was performed, and 15 proteins whose expression was significantly altered in both tumor types were identified. The obtained results confirm the effectiveness of the multiplex MRM MS approach for the quantitative analysis of protein biomarkers. Further research and validation on larger samples are required to evaluate the clinical significance and potential for implementing the developed method in laboratory diagnostics.

records.title: KIR3DL1-based inhibitory CAR NK cell therapy alleviates on-target, off-tumor toxicity with retention of antitumor effects
records.abstract: Background Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has significantly improved outcomes in hematologic malignancies. However, its translation to solid tumors is hampered by on-target, off-tumor toxicity (OTOT) and antigen escape. These obstacles underscore the need for novel strategies that enhance antitumor efficacy while limiting OTOT. Methods We designed a NOT logic-gated CAR natural killer (NK) cell architecture that targets B7H3, a tumor-associated antigen, and endomucin (EMCN), an antigen serving as a safety marker in normal tissues. These dual CAR NK cells selectively targeted and eliminated B7H3-high tumor cells, whereas their activation was suppressed upon encountering normal cell models co-expressing B7H3 and EMCN. A panel of inhibitory intracellular domains derived from T cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin and immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif domains (TIGIT), killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptors 2DL1 (KIR2DL1) and 3DL1 (KIR3DL1), and sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-like lectins 7 and 9 (Siglec-7/9) was screened to identify the optimal module for the EMCN-specific CAR NK cells. Results The dual CAR NK cells demonstrated precise tumor selectivity and markedly reduced OTOT relative to conventional B7H3-targeted CAR NK cells. The KIR3DL1 intracellular domain proved to be the most effective, robustly suppressing cytotoxicity upon recognition of EMCN on B7H3 + engineered SKOV3-EMCN cells and thereby conferring potent protection. records.title: Glioblastoma–Neuroblastoma Cocultured Multicellular Spheroid Model for Evaluating Temozolomide Response
affiliations: Advanced Centre for Treatment, Research and Education in Cancer
records.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most lethal primary brain tumor, and its resistance to therapy is increasingly understood to arise not from tumor cells alone but also from their integration into the surrounding neural circuitry. However, no existing preclinical spheroid model isolates the direct effect of neuronal-lineage cells on glioblastoma's drug response within a rapid, scalable 3D system. We developed a heterotypic 3D coculture spheroid combining glioblastoma (U87-MG) with a neuronal-lineage surrogate population (SH-SY5Y) via the agarose liquid overlay method to directly understand this gap. Subsequently, growth, morphology, hypoxia, and temozolomide (TMZ) response over 14 days against glioblastoma only and neuroblastoma only spheroids were characterized. The coculture adopted a glioblastoma like compact, chemoresistant architecture yet, contrary to what this architecture alone would predict, it showed measurable chemosensitivity at every TMZ concentration tested, including 10 µM, a dose at which neither monoculture responded at all. This indicates that the neuronal-lineage surrogate population alters the overall TMZ response of the coculture spheroids. Drug-response data from glioblastoma only models may therefore not reflect true tumor behavior in the presence of neuronal-lineage cells, supporting the inclusion of neuronal-lineage surrogate components in preclinical glioblastoma drug screening.

records.title: Green Tea Catechins in Cancer Prevention and Therapy: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, Safety, and Future Perspectives
records.journal: Asian Journal of Science Technology Engineering and Art
records.abstract: Green tea, derived from Camellia sinensis, is a widely consumed dietary source of bioactive polyphenols. Among its major catechins, epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) has been studied most extensively in cancer research. This review critically synthesizes phytochemical, molecular, preclinical, epidemiological, clinical, pharmacokinetic, and safety evidence to assess the potential role of green tea catechins in cancer prevention and treatment. Preclinical studies of breast, prostate, colorectal, lung, liver, oral, and hematological cancers indicate that EGCG modulates oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, proliferation, apoptosis, cell-cycle progression, angiogenesis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, invasion, metastasis, and epigenetic regulation. Reported molecular targets include the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, MAPK, JAK–STAT, and NF-κB signaling pathways, as well as EGFR and VEGF signaling, BCL-2 family proteins, caspases, matrix metalloproteinases, and enzymes involved in DNA methylation. A systematic review and meta-analysis reported an association between green tea or EGCG exposure and lower overall cancer risk, with variation by cancer type and study design. Clinical evidence for efficacy in established malignancies remains limited, and conventional oncological treatment remains the standard of care. records.title: Co-design and feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for colorectal cancer survivors: a mix-methods study
records.abstract: PURPOSE: Colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors experience persistent challenges that negatively affect health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While mobile health (mHealth) may offer a useful approach to survivorship care, limited user involvement and scarcity of structured programs in developing countries remain barriers. This study aimed to co-design and evaluate the feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for CRC survivors following primary treatment. METHODS: A mixed-methods study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 utilized a user-centered design framework involving 12 co-designers across nine online sessions to develop and refine the FORYOU mHealth program. Phase 2 was a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) with 30 CRC survivors to assess feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the 12-week program, measured by HRQoL outcomes. RESULTS: In phase 1, the co-designed program indicated above-average usability (System Usability Scale ≥ 68) and adequate acceptability (E-Acceptability Scale ≥ 24). In phase 2, the adherence rate was 73.3%; participants in the intervention group completed an average of 5.4 out of 6 sessions and accessed the app 9.7 times. Although no significant between-group difference was observed in overall HRQoL, exploratory findings were mixed. The intervention favored the subscale functional well-being (P < 0.05; g = 1.34), whereas the control group favored the secondary outcome, fatigue. records.abstract: Abstract Background Colorectal cancer survivors may experience persistent nutritional problems, but the association between their health-promoting behaviour patterns and nutritional risk is poorly understood. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study in a primary care setting in Shanghai, China. Latent profile analysis identified patterns of health-promoting behaviour, and logistic regression examined their associations with nutritional risk. Results Of 207 questionnaires distributed, 203 valid responses were analysed; 58.62% of participants were men and 60.1% were aged ≥ 70 years. Nutritional risk was present in 27.09% of participants, with prevalences of 42.2%, 18.7%, and 10.3% in the low-level, moderate-level, and high-level profiles, respectively (p < 0.001). Compared with the low-level profile, the moderate-level and high-level profiles had lower adjusted odds of nutritional risk (odds ratio [OR] 0.31, 95% CI 0.14–0.67; and OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02–0.34, respectively). Participants aged ≥ 70 years had higher odds than those aged ≤ 60 years (OR 5.25, 95% CI 1.21–33.41). A longer time since diagnosis was associated with lower odds of nutritional risk. Conclusions These findings suggest that survivors with low levels of health-promoting behaviour may warrant closer nutritional assessment in primary care. records.abstract: Nghiên cứu nhằm đánh giá mức độ chấp nhận và tính khả thi của việc lấy mẫu xét nghiệm HPV DNA trong sàng lọc ung thư cổ tử cung từ góc nhìn cán bộ y tế (CBYT) tuyến cơ sở tại Hải Phòng năm 2023. Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang, kết hợp định lượng và định tính, với khảo sát 30 CBYT và 8 cuộc thảo luận nhóm tại các trạm y tế thuộc huyện Thủy Nguyên và Vĩnh Bảo. Kết quả cho thấy 70,0% CBYT quen thuộc hoặc rất quen thuộc với phương pháp lấy mẫu. Tỷ lệ chấp nhận triển khai tại trạm y tế và tại cộng đồng lần lượt là 100,0% và 96,7%. Có 73,3% CBYT không ghi nhận khó khăn khi lấy mẫu; 93,3% đánh giá hệ thống dễ sử dụng, 93,3% tự tin khi sử dụng, nhưng 53,3% cho biết cần hỗ trợ kỹ thuật. Thảo luận nhóm ghi nhận những trở ngại liên quan đến việc phụ nữ tự lấy mẫu và nhu cầu hỗ trợ bảo quản, vận chuyển mẫu. Kết quả cho thấy mức độ chấp nhận cao và tính khả thi bước đầu từ góc nhìn CBYT. Việc mở rộng triển khai cần tăng cường đào tạo, hỗ trợ kỹ thuật, chuẩn hóa quy trình bảo quản, vận chuyển mẫu và truyền thông nâng cao nhận thức cộng đồng.

records.title: REG2024: a benchmark challenge and curated dataset for pathology report generation from giga- pixel whole-slide images of bladder cancer
records.abstract: Abstract Background We aimed to construct a curated whole-slide image (WSI)-report dataset for bladder cancer and establish a clinically grounded benchmark for evaluating vision–language models through an open community challenge. Methods We curated a dataset of 902 deidentified bladder cancer WSIs paired with corresponding pathology reports. Seven teams submitted distinct modeling frameworks. Performance was assessed using a clinically weighted composite metric integrating word-overlap scores (ROUGE-L, BLEU-4), keyword matching, and embedding-based semantic similarity. Expert mean opinion scores (MOS) were obtained, and the correlation between the weighted-sum score and expert-assigned MOS was analyzed. Results Two modeling strategies emerged: end-to-end generative architectures and multi-step classification-then-generation pipelines. Among individual submissions, the top-ranked multi-step pipeline achieved the highest main-diagnosis accuracy (48/50), whereas end-to-end models showed greater sensitivity to rare pathological features. The weighted-sum metric correlated strongly with MOS within each team (Spearman’s ρ, 0.65–0.91) and, on reports with clinically important misclassifications, agreed with MOS more closely than any single metric. Conclusions Performance variability was influenced by architectural design and the integration of pretrained foundation models. Our proposed evaluation framework addressed key limitations of conventional natural language processing metric

records.title: Multicenter CT-Based Deep Learning for Preoperative Nodal Risk Stratification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University
records.abstract: Background: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses. Methods: A total of 1560 patients with PTC from six hospitals were retrospectively included. The Tongji Hospital cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets, and five external cohorts were used for independent testing. Seven 2.5D tumor slices were extracted per patient, encoded with a DenseNet201 backbone, and fused by a Transformer. Model performance was compared with radiomics, ensemble learning, and multi-instance learning using AUC, calibration, decision curve, and precision-recall analyses. Bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics were used to explore related biological features. Results: ThyLNT achieved an AUC of 0.882 (CI, 0.858–0.905) in the training cohort, 0.787 (CI, 0.738–0.835) in the internal validation cohort, and 0.772 (CI, 0.662–0.878) to 0.827 (CI, 0.763–0.885) across the five external cohorts. It showed multicenter discrimination, whereas calibration and threshold-dependent operating characteristics varied across cohorts. records.journal: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng
records.abstract: Nghiên cứu nhằm mô tả chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh sau phẫu thuật ung thư tuyến giáp tại Bệnh viện Nội tiết Trung ương năm 2026. Sử dụng thiết kế mô tả cắt ngang sử dụng bộ câu hỏi EORTC QLQ-C30 và THY-34 phỏng vấn 181 người bệnh ung thư tuyến giáp đã được phẫu thuật và hiện đang khám theo dõi định kỳ tại khoa Khám bệnh, Bệnh viện Nội tiết trung ương từ 01/2026-06/2026. Đối tượng nghiên cứu chủ yếu là nữ giới (86,2%), tuổi trung bình 45,1 ± 10,9; đa số mắc ung thư tuyến giáp thể nhú giai đoạn I (97,8%). Theo thang đo EORTC QLQ-C30, các lĩnh vực chức năng đạt điểm tương đối cao (75,9–85,2 điểm), điểm sức khỏe tổng quát đạt 69,1 ± 14,1; các triệu chứng nổi bật là mệt mỏi (24,3 ± 18,3), rối loạn giấc ngủ (22,7 ± 25,0) và đau (18,1 ± 16,9). Theo thang đo EORTC QLQ THY-34, các lĩnh vực có điểm cao nhất là hỗ trợ xã hội (80,9 ± 23,7), tác động xã hội (56,0 ± 29,2) và triệu chứng cảm xúc (48,5 ± 22,8); các triệu chứng đặc hiệu thường gặp nhất là triệu chứng vùng cổ (26,3 ± 17,4), vấn đề về giọng nói (21,2 ± 18,6) và khó nuốt (18,3 ± 19,0). Chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh sau phẫu thuật ung thư tuyến giáp nhìn chung tương đối tốt, tuy nhiên vẫn cần quan tâm cải thiện các triệu chứng thể chất, tâm lý và xã hội.

affiliations: Institute of Social and Preventive Medicine
records.abstract: Abstract Background : Cardiotoxic effects of childhood cancer treatment on the right ventricle (RV) are sparsely studied among long-term childhood cancer survivors (CCS). Objectives : We investigated RV function and risk factors for impaired function. Methods : We invited CCS ≥18 years of age, diagnosed between ages 0–20 years, treated in one of five pediatric oncology centers across Switzerland from 1976–2017, who survived ≥5 years, for an echocardiographic assessment of the RV including tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE, abnormal <17mm) and Doppler tissue imaging (DTI, abnormal <9.5cm/s). Results : We included 432 CCS with median age at study of 34 years (interquartile range 26–40). records.abstract: Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae (Mhp) is a major cause of enzootic pneumonia in pigs, yet the molecular and spatial determinants underlying breed-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics and N-glycoproteomics to compare lung responses to experimental Mhp infection in Chenghua pigs with higher susceptibility and Yorkshire pigs with relative resilience. Under an identical inoculation dose, Chenghua pigs exhibited more severe clinical and pathological manifestations than Yorkshire pigs, despite comparable pulmonary Mhp loads at this late stage of infection. This observation suggests that disease severity is associated with differences in host response organization rather than with overall pathogen burden. Spatial analyses revealed a shared spatial and cellular infection framework across breeds, with marked differences in regulatory balance. Across spatial clusters, Chenghua pigs exhibited coordinated activation of TNF-α-NF-κB and IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, accompanied by relative attenuation of IFN-I responses. These inflammatory features co-occurred with hypoxia- and mTORC1-related metabolic reprogramming, activation of stress-response pathways, and engagement of tissue remodeling programmes. Transcription factor analyses further indicated increased activity of HIF1A, RELA and STAT3, together with reduced IRF9/STAT2-associated regulatory activity. records.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is critical for the induction of type I IFN (IFN I) and inflammatory responses against viral infection. The activity of STING is tightly regulated by various post-translational modifications (PTMs) to effectively defend against viral infection or prevent excessive immune responses. However, the regulatory mechanisms of STING activity remain largely unknown in teleost. In this study, we discovered that zebrafish death-associated protein kinase 3 (DAPK3) enhances the STING-mediated antiviral innate immune response through two synergistic mechanisms: the induction of an interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3)-dependent IFN I response and a nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-dependent pro-inflammatory cytokine response. Detailedly, viral stimulation triggers the expression of DAPK3, resulting in its autophosphorylation at Ser21 and Thr87. Activated DAPK3 subsequently interacts with STING, promoting its phosphorylation. Moreover, DAPK3 also recruits tripartite motif-containing protein 32 (TRIM32), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, then increases K63-linked polyubiquitination of STING. Subsequently, activated STING orchestrates two key responses: (i) it recruits TBK1 to enhance IRF3 phosphorylation and dimerization, thereby promoting IFN I production; (ii) it recruits the IKK complex (IKKα/IKKβ) to activate p65-mediated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TNFα), ultimately inducing apoptosis. records.abstract: Macrophages are highly heterogeneous immune cells with context-dependent functions, yet their transcriptional, functional, and metabolic diversity across prenatal tissues of the whole body, sexes and stages remains elusive. During fetal development, macrophages play essential roles in tissue formation and maintaining maternal-fetal immune balance, but their specific phenotypic and functional changes in the context of fetal growth restriction remain relatively underexplored. Herein, we constructed a single-cell cross-tissue macrophage atlas comprising 85,473 cells from 54 tissues of late-gestation fetal pigs. Analysis identified 15 macrophage subtypes, among which two Hofbauer cell subtypes were distinguished by their distinct transcriptional and functional characteristics between the amniotic and chorioallantoic membranes: the HBC GPNMB+ subtype upregulated glycolytic enzymes and extracellular matrix regulators such as LDHA and GPNMB, whereas the HBC PEG10+ subtype highly expressed immunomodulators and developmental regulators including A2M and PEG10. Two dichotomous subtypes, LYVE1highMHCIIlow and LYVE1lowMHCIIhigh, were systematically delineated across 27 tissues, and a core transcriptional signature distinguishing them was defined in both pig and human. This review critically evaluates animal models, conventional cell systems, induced pluripotent stem cell models, and organoids of WD, with an emphasis on the phenotypes reproduced, experimental strengths and limitations, and translational applications of each platform. records.abstract: Placental hypertrophy is a major cause of pregnancy failure in somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) animals, with metabolic-epigenetic crosstalk proposed as a key regulatory node, yet its molecular mechanism remains elusive. Isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (Idh2) is a critical mitochondrial metabolic enzyme that controls the production of α-Ketoglutarate (α-KG), a central regulator of epigenetic modifications. In SCNT bovine placentomes and derived placental mesenchymal cells, this study found abnormally elevated α-KG levels. Further functional experiments in these cells suggested that elevated α-KG levels were associated with significant increases in 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) and the active histone marker H3K4me3, as well as decreases in the repressive markers H3K9me3 and H3K27me3, accompanied by altered expression of ten-eleven translocation (TET) dioxygenases and lysine demethylase (KDMs). This ultimately led to the dysregulation of key imprinted genes associated with placental development, including upregulation of Igf2r and Znf597, and downregulation of Phlda2, Peg10, and Magel2. Further analysis revealed that Idh2, a key enzyme for α-KG synthesis, was significantly upregulated in SCNT bovine placentas, with tis promoter region exhibiting hypomethylation, increased H3K4me3 modification, and enhanced chromatin accessibility.
