records.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence associating circRNAs with candidate biomarker potential for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. records.abstract: Childhood cancers are life-threatening diseases and are a major cause of death in children worldwide. Research shows that children with cancer are at risk for psychopathology, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety and depression. Major theories of psychopathology assign a significant role to the way people attend to and remember negative content as predictors and maintenance factors in emotional disorders. Thus, the aim of the proposed research is to delineate factors that may predict psychopathology among children with cancer. In line with central theories of emotional disorders (Mathews & MacLeod, 2005), we focus on cognitive biases involving processing threat-related information, and their relation to psychopathology. Biases will involve stimuli related with cancer, non-cancer negative and neutral. These types of stimuli were chosen to explore whether the biases are specific to stimuli that are related to the acquired illness. Subsequently, they will be interviewed using semi-structured clinical interviews to assess the presence of emotional disorders. Finally, they will complete a set of questionnaires assessing symptom severity of depression, anxiety, and PTSD. For a control group we will have a healthy children group. records.title: Molecular determinants of antibody-mediated priming to enhance detection of ctDNA
affiliations: Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research At MIT
records.abstract: PURPOSE: Liquid biopsies can enable cancer detection and monitoring yet remain limited by low amounts of ctDNA. To address this limitation, we previously introduced a monoclonal antibody (mAb) "priming agent" that transiently increased the amount of ctDNA in blood. Here, we investigated the molecular features in both the agent and the target that drive this effect. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We developed a panel of novel mAbs and other cfDNA-binding agents and characterized their interaction with cfDNA, impact on cfDNA clearance, ability to increase ctDNA recovery, and impact on cfDNA fragmentation and composition in tumor bearing mice. RESULTS: mAbs targeting either dsDNA or intact mononucleosomes increased the recovery of cfDNA and ctDNA without changing tumor fraction. mAbs with high avidity to dsDNA performed best, highlighting dsDNA as the key structural target for priming agents. One agent preserved short molecules of cfDNA associated with transcription factor binding sites and typically depleted at baseline. The Fc domain was not required for a measurable priming effect, as F(ab')2 retained priming activity. Leveraging these insights, we engineered single-chain agents using the dsDNA binding domain sso7d, expanding priming strategies beyond immunoglobulins. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the molecular features and general design principles for mAb-based priming agents to enhance recovery and detection of ctDNA.

records.title: Engineering signal transduction for closed-loop gene and cell therapies
records.abstract: Chronic diseases are still treated largely with interventions that are constitutive, intermittently administered and poorly aligned with real-time physiology. Synthetic biology is changing this paradigm by treating gene circuits as programmable genetic software that can be deployed across cellular therapeutic hardware spanning from prokaryotic to eukaryotic systems, including probiotic cells, designer cells, immune cells and stem‑cell‑derived platforms. In this framework, engineered systems can sense disease-associated signals, compute them through synthetic or repurposed transduction pathways and adjust therapeutic output to maintain physiological variables within a desired range. Closed-loop therapeutics therefore begin to merge diagnosis, treatment and prevention within the same living platform. Across metabolism, inflammation, infection, cardiovascular regulation and cancer, early mammalian systems show that endogenous sensing, intracellular computation and therapeutic actuation can be combined in clinically relevant architectures. The emerging concept of setpoint medicine captures the clinical ambition of these systems: not simply to deliver a dose, but to keep physiology within an interpretable and therapeutically desirable range. Realizing this vision will require durable and modular control circuits, hardware-aware delivery strategies, interpretable safety frameworks, controller-style performance metrics and increasingly AI-assisted design, calibration and oversight.

affiliations: Academic Center for Education, Culture and Research
records.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, driven largely by tumor heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and therapeutic resistance. Tissue biopsy, while the diagnostic gold standard, offers only a static snapshot of a constantly evolving disease, and repeated sampling is often impractical, particularly in metastatic settings. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative capable of capturing this evolving biology in real time through circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells (CTCs), and extracellular vesicles (EVs). This review examines the biological features, analytical technologies, and clinical applications of these analytes in BC, with particular attention to two rapidly evolving areas. First, we discuss how artificial intelligence and machine learning are being applied to multi-analyte liquid biopsy data, from methylation- and fragmentomics-based classifiers for early detection to models integrating ctDNA and CTC information for resistance profiling and treatment-response prediction, while critically examining current limits in clinical validation and interpretability. records.title: Long-standing Chronic Diarrhea Associated With Intestinal Spirochetosis Incidentally Diagnosed in a Rectal Adenoma Specimen Resected by Cold Snare Polypectomy: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Endoscopy Aichi Cancer Center Hospital Aichi Japan.
records.abstract: Intestinal spirochetosis (IS) is an uncommon condition that is often asymptomatic and detected incidentally but may occasionally present with chronic diarrhea. We report a case of IS incidentally identified in the adjacent non-neoplastic mucosa of a rectal adenoma specimen resected by cold snare polypectomy. We present a case of a man in his 50s who was referred for a positive fecal occult blood test and had a history of chronic diarrhea. Colonoscopy revealed a 5-mm sessile polyp in the upper rectum, which was removed by cold snare polypectomy. Histopathological examination showed a tubular adenoma. In addition, routine hematoxylin and eosin staining revealed a characteristic false brush border on the adjacent non-neoplastic colorectal epithelium, consistent with IS. A detailed medical interview subsequently revealed chronic diarrhea for more than 10 years and prolonged close contact with a pet dog. Treatment with metronidazole (1500 mg/day for 10 days) resulted in resolution of the diarrhea. This case highlights the importance of careful histopathological examination and detailed history-taking in patients with IS.

records.title: Disparities across Colorectal Cancer Screening Modalities: Recommendations and Uptake
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second leading cause of cancer death in the United States, with persistent disparities in screening rates. We examined racial and ethnic disparities in provider recommendations for CRC screening tests and screening uptake among U.S. adults eligible for screening using cross-sectional data from the 2019, 2021, and 2023 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Participants included adults aged 50-75 in 2019/2021 and 45-75 in 2023 (N=39,771). Primary outcomes were self-reported provider recommendation in the past 12 months and up-to-date status with guideline-concordant screening. In fully adjusted models accounting for socioeconomic factors and insurance, Hispanic (aOR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.56-0.82), non-Hispanic Black (aOR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.67-0.98), and non-Hispanic Asian adults (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.38-0.66) were significantly less likely than non-Hispanic White adults to receive recommendations. Odds of being up to date were lower for Hispanic (aOR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.75-0.93), Asian (aOR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.51-0.68), and American Indian/Alaska Native adults (aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.55-0.96). Difference-in-differences analysis confirmed that the 2021 recommendations change increased provider recommendations by 13.4 percentage points among 45-49 year-olds. Persistent disparities in recommendation patterns highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve equity.

records.title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
records.abstract: Abstract Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

records.title: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
records.abstract: Abstract Background An important application of single-cell genomics experiments is to identify genes specific to biological categories or experimental conditions. We develop ember (Entropy Metrics for Biological ExploRation), an entropy-based framework that uses Shannon’s chain rule across nested biological partitions. Four axioms characterize its Ψ score within a class of normalized entropy-decomposition scores. Results Applying ember to eight tissues from eight founder mouse strains, we find that gene specificity is often unintuitive: canonical markers can be supplanted, housekeeping genes are context-dependent, and mouse strain can drive unexpected cell type switching. Unsupervised learning on entropy metrics uncovers shared genes specialized to male gonads and kidney, as well as genes specific to non-consecutive developmental stages in the kidney. To facilitate further exploration of gene specificity in mice, we have also developed a comprehensive specificity database, along with a web interface, API and MCP server. Extending ember to a human PBMC dataset collected from 255 diverse individuals, we find that variation in PBMCs is largely localized to classical monocytes. We also find genes with unique specificity by sex, age and ancestral background. Conclusions Together, these applications establish ember as a powerful tool and provide a roadmap for elucidating the impact of human genetic variation using the murine model.

records.title: Arctic Puffin Algorithm with local escaping operator for feature selection in high-dimensional datasets
records.abstract: Abstract Large datasets might make data mining more difficult due to their high dimensionality. To minimize the dimensionality of large datasets, feature selection is an essential step that maximizes classification accuracy by choosing the most informative features. In this study, a binary adaptation of the enhanced Arctic Puffin Optimization (EAPO) algorithm, which builds on the Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO) algorithm, is introduced within a wrapper-based framework to identify the optimal subset of features for classification tasks. To improve the search performance of APO, a local escaping operator is incorporated to effectively balance exploration and exploitation and enhance its ability to escape local optima. Furthermore, a key aspect of EAPO is the design of the transfer function, which facilitates the transformation of the continuous search space into a binary domain. To evaluate its effectiveness, three transfer functions, S-shaped, V-shaped, and U-shaped, are investigated. The proposed EAPO method is assessed on 14 benchmark datasets using the k-Nearest Neighbor classifier as the evaluation metric. To control overfitting, k-fold cross-validation employs a partitioning strategy in which the dataset is divided into k folds, and each fold is used as the test set once while the remaining folds form the training set. records.title: Lipid Metabolic Rewiring in Cancer Drug Resistance: Pathways, Networks, and Therapeutic Strategies
records.abstract: Drug resistance limits cancer therapy, and metabolic reprogramming helps tumor cells adapt to therapeutic stress. This review examines how altered lipid uptake, synthesis, storage, and oxidation support survival by changing signaling, membrane composition, energy production, redox balance, and tumor-microenvironment interactions. The SCAP/SREBP axis is a key transcriptional regulator; oncogenic and nutrient signaling (EGFR, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, mutant p53) controls SREBP abundance and activation, and sustained SREBP activity during treatment distinguishes resistant from sensitive cells in several models, including gefitinib-resistant lung cancer and sorafenib/lenvatinib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MicroRNAs regulate these pathways post-transcriptionally, including ferroptosis-related targets (ACSL4, SLC7A11, GPX4). Inhibitors of lipogenesis, SCAP/SREBP, cholesterol metabolism, fatty-acid oxidation, lipid uptake and storage, phospholipid and sphingolipid signaling, and ferroptosis have improved drug sensitivity in preclinical models. However, many studies show only an association with resistance rather than that modulating a pathway restores sensitivity; findings vary between tumor types; and compensatory rewiring, toxicity, and limited tumor selectivity constrain single-target approaches, while miRNA-based therapeutics remain early-stage. Rational combinations guided by lipidomic and transcriptomic profiling are a priority.

records.abstract: Abstract Background HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV OPSCC) has excellent cure rates with standard high-dose radiation therapy (RT) and chemotherapy, but this comes at the cost of substantial long-term toxicity. records.title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
records.abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. records.abstract: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. records.title: Interactions Between Cancer and the Nervous System: a Review of Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities in Cancer Neuroscience
affiliations: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review The emerging field of cancer neuroscience investigates how neural activity shapes tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. Recent research aims to define the bidirectional communication between neurons, glial cells, and tumor cells, and to clarify how neural signals influence the tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent Findings Neuronal activity promotes glioma growth via paracrine mediators such as neuroligin-3 (NLGN3), BDNF, TSP-1 and IGF-1, activating PI3K–mTOR signaling and supporting tumor proliferation. Cancer cells also exploit glutamatergic synapses, with AMPA and NMDA receptor activity driving survival and invasion, suggesting opportunities for repurposing antiseizure drugs such as perampanel. Ionic signaling through K⁺ and Ca²⁺ channels further facilitate tumor–neuron coupling. Beyond gliomas, sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs, as well as chronic stress–induced HPA axis activation, modulate angiogenesis, immune evasion, and metastasis. Summary Neural regulation of cancer encompasses neurotrophic signaling, neurotransmitter pathways, ion channel activity, and stress-mediated neuroendocrine responses, collectively shaping tumor biology and revealing novel therapeutic targets.

records.title: Attention guided segmentation and multi resolution transformer learning for blood cancer detection
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose Blood cell cancers, including leukemia, lymphoma, and multiple myeloma, disrupt the hematopoietic system, necessitating precise and early diagnosis for effective treatment. Traditional diagnostic methods face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, and real-time applicability. Approach This study presents an integrated framework combining attention-guided segmentation, multi-resolution transformer-based feature extraction, and attention-enhanced classification for blood-cell image analysis. Using a publicly sourced dataset of 500 class-labelled blood-smear images, the framework incorporates UNet++ with Attention Gates for segmentation, multi-resolution DeiT for feature extraction, and AE-MLP for AML, ALL, and healthy-cell classification. Results The final attention-guided UNet++ configuration achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.95, an IoU of 0.88, precision of 0.96, recall of 0.93, and pixel-level segmentation accuracy of 0.97. Multi-resolution DeiT representation learning was associated with improved boundary delineation relative to the evaluated segmentation comparators and achieved a mean Grad-CAM-based Attention Focus Score of 92.4%, indicating that 92.4% of the normalized class-associated activation was concentrated within the designated cellular region. The AE-MLP classification stage achieved an overall accuracy of 96.0%, a rare blast-cell sensitivity of 94.7%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.95. records.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
records.abstract: Ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury involves multiple interconnected mechanisms, including mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening and ferroptosis, whereas calcium overload and reactive oxygen species generation act as upstream injury signals rather than independent forms of regulated cell death. Cuproptosis is, at present, a weakly evidenced emerging candidate rather than a core mechanism on par with ferroptosis. Rather than centring cuproptosis, this review proposes a falsifiable metabolic-susceptibility framework and grades the existing evidence honestly. Its central premise is the dependence of cuproptosis on mitochondrial respiration and lipoylated metabolic proteins. During ischemia, suppression of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) activity and oxidative metabolism may reduce cuproptosis susceptibility without necessarily diminishing DLAT lipoylation. During reperfusion, partial recovery of mitochondrial metabolism may create permissive conditions for copper-dependent proteotoxicity against a dynamically evolving background of oxidative stress, calcium dysregulation, and inflammation. This proposed transition remains hypothetical, as direct time-resolved evidence is limited and neither uniform susceptibility nor synchronized cuproptosis activation has been established. affiliations: Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University
records.abstract: Background Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are innate-like T lymphocytes that bridge innate and adaptive immunity. While their dysfunction is implicated in various cancers, their role in multiple myeloma (MM), particularly the dominant CD8 + MAIT subset, remains poorly defined. Objective To investigate the frequency, phenotype, function, and clinical relevance of MAIT cells, with a focus on CD8 + MAIT cells, in MM patients. Methods We analyzed peripheral blood (PB) and bone marrow (BM) samples from 120 MM patients (77 newly diagnosed, 22 in remission, 21 relapsed) and 30 healthy controls (HCs) using multi-color flow cytometry to assess MAIT cell frequency, subset distribution, activation (programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) expression), and effector function (cytokine production and cytotoxic molecule expression). Clinical parameters and survival outcomes were correlated with MAIT cell levels. Results MM patients demonstrated a significant reduction in total MAIT cell frequency, driven primarily by a loss of CD8 + MAIT cells. These cells exhibited a functional dysfunction phenotype marked by PD-1 upregulation. Functionally, they showed impaired production of interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) upon activation but elevated constitutive expression of granzyme B and perforin. records.title: The MAGOH/hnRNPH1 axis promotes alternative splicing-derived soluble PD-L1 generation and attenuates PD-L1 blockade efficacy in gastric cancer
records.abstract: Abstract Despite the clinical success of PD-1 blockade, the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in gastric cancer (GC) remains limited. Soluble PD-L1 (sPD-L1) has been proposed to function as a decoy that sequesters anti-PD-L1 antibodies, potentially contributing to therapeutic resistance. Our previous study identified an exon 5/6-skipping PD-L1 splice variant, designated PD-L1-v1, as an important source of sPD-L1 in GC. We also found that MAGOH is highly expressed in GC and participates in alternative splicing regulation. Here, we demonstrate that PD-L1-v1 acts as a soluble decoy that limits PD-L1 blocker binding to membrane-bound PD-L1 on tumor cells, thereby impairing the antitumor efficacy of PD-L1 blockade. Mechanistically, MAGOH upregulates hnRNPH1 expression, primarily by enhancing its mRNA stability, and promotes hnRNPH1-dependent exon5/6 skipping of PD-L1 pre-mRNA, thereby facilitating PD-L1-v1 and sPD-L1 generation. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism of resistance to PD-L1 blockade and highlight the MAGOH/hnRNPH1 axis as a potential strategy for improving immunotherapy efficacy in GC.

records.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer
records.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outlines current computational and experimental techniques to identify, prioritise, and functionally validate non-coding variants in PDAC. We discuss in silico methods including genome-wide association study (GWAS) fine-mapping, colocalisation, machine learning-driven functional annotation, and the use of established computational tools, in addition to epigenomic profiling technologies including, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and CUT&RUN which define regulatory landscapes. We also emphasise new AI-based methods involving radiogenomics, AI imaging analysis and data integration, which provides novel potential to link genomic variation with phenotypic and imaging characteristics. records.title: [Emphasis on the standardization of initial treatment for ovarian cancer].
records.abstract: Based on the current technical development status among various regions and medical institutions in China, this article proposes corresponding clinical decision-making pathways to standardize and homogenize the initial treatment of ovarian cancer and optimize patient prognosis. All patients require comprehensive and thorough evaluation by the gynecologic oncology multidisciplinary team. Comprehensive staging surgery is indicated for early-stage ovarian cancer. For advanced cases, primary debulking surgery or interval debulking surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is adopted based on clinical indications, with great emphasis on multidisciplinary expertise and surgical quality to elevate the implementation rate and complete resection rate of the initial debulking surgery. Standard first-line chemotherapy with adequate dosage and full cycles is strongly recommended. For advanced patients who have achieved remission after chemotherapy, genetic testing-guided maintenance therapy is preferred. Regular post-treatment follow-up is essential for early identification of tumor recurrence.

affiliations: University of Florida Health Science Center
records.abstract: Copy number variants (CNVs) are prevalent in both diploid and haploid genomes and contribute to genome evolution and phenotypic diversity. However, CNV detection in low-input data, including low-cell and single-cell sequencing data, remains challenging due to the shallow and highly uneven read counts and amplification bias. Another challenge lies in selecting reference samples, which are used to provide a baseline for defining copy-number losses or gains. Normalization using references containing common CNVs can lead to cancellation of true CNV signals or false CNV calls. Here, we develop GapCNV, a statistical framework for CNV detection in low-input DNA sequencing data from both haploid and diploid genomes. GapCNV uses preliminary cell clustering and shared CNV profiles to construct bin-specific pseudo-references from cells inferred to have the copy-neutral state. This strategy reduces the incorporation of common CNVs into the normalization baseline and thereby preserves common CNV signals. We evaluated GapCNV using simulations with and without amplification biases and datasets from Plasmodium falciparum , human breast cancer and melanoma. In simulations, GapCNV achieved high precision rate while maintaining competitive sensitivity, with advantages for detecting short and common CNVs. records.title: Echidna: a Bayesian framework for integrative inference of copy number alterations impacting phenotypic plasticity
records.abstract: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms. Echidna integrates genomic and transcriptomics data to reveal how copy number alterations shape tumor evolution and therapy resistance.

records.title: Rank-One Convexification for Quadratic Optimization Problems with Switching Constraints
records.abstract: We investigate convexification for convex quadratic optimization with switching constraints. Such problems can be cast as mixed-integer quadratic optimization problems, where binary variables are used to encode whether a linear inequality is active or not. First, we derive the convex hull for the epigraph of a quadratic function defined by a rank-one matrix and switching penalties. Using this rank-one convexification, we develop copositive and semidefinite relaxations for general convex quadratic functions. Leveraging these findings, we construct convex formulations to the support vector machine problem with 0–1 loss. The resulting methods scale well with the number of data points, provided that the number of features is small. In terms of statistical performance, the proposed methods outperform standard support vector machine problems with hinge loss in data sets corrupted by outliers. Funding: A. Gómez and S. records.title: Corilagin increases the sensitivity of neuroblastoma to cisplatin by regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
records.abstract: Drug resistance remains the leading cause of cisplatin treatment failure in neuroblastoma (NB). This study aimed to investigate the potential of corilagin as an adjuvant therapy for overcoming cisplatin resistance in NB. In vitro functional assays—including cell viability (CCK-8), colony formation, transwell migration, and invasion assays—were conducted to evaluate the effects of corilagin in combination with cisplatin on human NB cell lines (SH-SY5Y and SK-N-BE(2)) and a cisplatin-resistant subline (SH-SY5Y/R). In vivo tumorigenesis experiments were performed to assess the suppressive effects of the corilagin-cisplatin combination on tumor growth initiated by SH-SY5Y and SH-SY5Y/R cells in mouse models. RNA sequencing was utilized to identify molecular mechanisms associated with cisplatin resistance and the therapeutic action of corilagin, followed by functional validation using 740Y-P, a specific agonist of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Our results showed that the combination of corilagin and cisplatin significantly inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion, and autophagic activity in SH-SY5Y/R cells, while robustly inducing apoptosis. Importantly, the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was found to be hyperactivated during the development of cisplatin resistance, whereas corilagin effectively suppressed this activation. These findings indicate that corilagin enhances cisplatin sensitivity in NB cells through modulation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

records.title: Laboratory Models of Hepatitis B and D Viruses: Search for Cell Permissiveness and Restriction Factors
records.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is an oncogenic human pathogen that accounts for 250 mln cases of chronic hepatitis worldwide. Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) is its satellite that substantially aggravates liver disease. The development of new antivirals and the investigation of viral pathogenesis are limited by the absence of effective cellular and animal models. Current cell models are based on human primary hepatocytes, liver progenitor HepaRG cells, iPS-derived hepatocyte-like cells or various hepatoma cells overexpressing the putative NTCP receptor. However, in most of these models, a majority of cells are non-permissive. In this review, we briefly assess these models, summarize the approaches to the increasing infection rates, and discuss the data on proviral and antiviral (restriction) host factors. The data discussed suggest that rates of HBV and HDV infections are limited by hepatocyte polarization and insufficient expression of the NTCP receptor, as well as the existence of additional co-receptors and restriction factors that can act mostly on the virus entry stage.

records.title: TIPE2 suppresses adipogenesis via METTL14-mediated m6A methylation and represents a potential therapeutic target for obesity
records.abstract: Abstract Despite conserved mechanisms maintaining energy homeostasis, the global obesity epidemic continues to rise. Tumor necrosis factor-α-induced protein 8-like 2 (TIPE2) is an anti-inflammatory regulator essential for immune homeostasis, yet its role in adipogenesis remains unclear. Here, we show that TIPE2 expression in human adipose tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index (BMI) and metabolic dysfunction. In mice, Tipe2 deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity, hyperglycaemia, and insulin resistance, whereas systemic AAV-mediated TIPE2 overexpression alleviates these phenotypes. In vitro, TIPE2 suppresses adipogenic differentiation in primary preadipocytes. Mechanistically, TIPE2 regulates N6-methyladenosine (m6A) via m6A methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14). Loss of TIPE2 reduces m6A levels and METTL14 expression, whereas METTL14 restoration reverses the pro-adipogenic effects. Furthermore, TIPE2 modulates adipogenesis through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) signaling. Together, these findings identify TIPE2 as a suppressor of adipogenesis via coordinated regulation of METTL14-dependent m6A modification and PPAR-γ signaling.

records.title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
records.abstract: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR–Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression. Superb-seq integrates CRISPR–Cas9, T7 in situ transcription and scRNA-seq to capture genome edits and gene expression in single cells.

records.title: 4D mitochondrial network assumes distinct and predictive phenotypes through human lung and intestinal epithelial development
records.abstract: Abstract Mitochondria form dynamic three-dimensional networks that exhibit a wide range of morphology and motility depending on cell state, cell type, and cell fate. Isolated phenotypes have been described for individual cell states, but how mitochondrial morphology and motility change across the full course of human tissue development has so far been unclear. Human stem cell-derived branching lung and intestinal organoids mimic developing human organs and make these systems accessible. Here we show, by imaging at key developmental time points from human stem cell through mature organoid tissue with lattice light-sheet microscopy, that mitochondrial networks adopt morphology and motility signatures that vary with developmental stage, that mitochondrial and cellular features can be used to predict developmental stage, and that two-dimensional measurements obscure features resolved only in three dimensions over time, yielding an integrated map of mitochondrial phenotypes across human tissue development.

records.abstract: Abstract Identifying malignant cells in single-cell gene expression data is essential for understanding tumor heterogeneity, but existing computational methods can be slow and perform inconsistently across datasets. Here, we present InferPloidy, a framework that combines graph-based cell grouping with iterative probabilistic modeling to distinguish cells with normal and altered chromosome copy numbers using profiles generated by InferCNV. Across breast, lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer datasets, the evaluated workflow reduces computation time by up to two orders of magnitude compared with existing tools and improves agreement with published cell annotations. This classification supports the identification of established therapeutic targets and candidate cell surface markers associated with tumor subtypes. The low proportion of unclassified cells helps preserve information for downstream analyses of gene expression differences and tumor population characteristics. These findings support InferPloidy as an efficient framework for tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery within the evaluated workflow. Its performance with inputs from other copy number inference methods requires further validation.

records.title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics
records.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. We present SVP, a framework that directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and regulatory programs from spatial transcriptomic data. SVP combines location-level functional activity inference with global and local spatial autocorrelation and extends these analyses to bivariate spatial coupling across heterogeneous features. Across simulations and real datasets, SVP recovered cell-state-associated activity patterns at individual captured locations, detected spatially variable features with calibrated statistics, and scaled efficiently to large datasets. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, SVP identified a spatially co-organized hypoxic and extracellular-matrix-remodeling niche that co-localized with regions of low immune activity. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque-associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. SVP enables direct analysis of functional spatial organization, moving beyond gene-centric descriptions of tissue structure.

records.abstract: Background The impact of clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), a novel cardiovascular risk factor, remains unclear in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), where cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the main cause of mortality. Methods We analysed data from 140,086 UK Biobank participants with MASLD. CHIP was identified via whole-exome sequencing. Incident CVD, including coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, and heart failure (HF), was the primary outcome. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between CHIP and CVD risk. Results During a median 13.5-year follow-up, 15.7% of participants developed CVD. CHIP was associated with a higher risk of CVD (HR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09–1.23), with higher risks of stroke (HR: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.07–1.38) and HF (HR: 1.34, 95% CI: 1.21–1.49). Mutations in ASXL1, SRSF2, JAK2 , and SF3B1 were associated with a particularly high CVD risk. Additionally, a higher clonal haematopoiesis risk score (CHRS) was associated with incident CVD, CHD, stroke, and HF. In the three-category analysis, the P value for trend was significant for all outcomes, but the association was confined to large CHIP for CVD and CHD, whereas both CHIP categories showed elevated estimates for stroke and HF. Conclusions CHIP is independently associated with incident CVD in patients with MASLD. These findings support prospective evaluation of CHIP-informed cardiovascular risk stratification in this population.

records.title: Exploratory analysis of CT-derived radiomic features and adipose tissue distribution in relation to lipid metabolism pathway activity in ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma
records.journal: Eurasian Journal of Medicine and Oncology
records.abstract: Introduction: Ovarian cancer is characterized by high recurrence rates and complex metabolic reprogramming. Lipid metabolism pathways may influence tumor imaging phenotypes and contribute to biologic heterogeneity. Objective: This study investigated whether computed tomography (CT)-derived radiomic features are associated with metabolic activity profiles in ovarian cancer. Methods: This retrospective radiogenomic study included 68 patients from the Cancer Genome Atlas Ovarian Cancer cohort with available contrast-enhanced CT imaging and matched transcriptomic data. Patients were stratified into high and low metabolic activity groups according to lipid metabolism-related pathway expression profiles. A two-dimensional radiomic approach was adopted using the axial CT slice showing the largest tumor area. Tumor regions were manually segmented, and handcrafted radiomic features were extracted using a custom pipeline developed in Python. Statistical comparisons between groups were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Results: Several radiomic features showed nominal or borderline differences between high- and low-metabolic-activity groups, including glcm_ASM_std (p = 0.027), shape_perimeter_mm (p = 0.045), glrlm_rln (p = 0.049), shape_minor_axis_length_px (p = 0.050), and intensity_p10_HU (p = 0.053). Tumors with higher metabolic activity tended to exhibit larger morphologic dimensions and subtle texture alterations.

records.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma • SFPQ/PSF-TFE3 renal cell carcinoma Symptoms: Hematuria • recurrent urinary tract infections • urinary urgency • weight loss Clinical Procedure: -Specialty: PathologyObjective: Rare disease Background:Transcription factor E3 (TFE3)-rearranged renal cell carcinoma is a rare subtype of renal tumor that relatively more frequent in the pediatric population.Histologically, it typically presents as a papillary neoplasm composed of clear epithelial cells with numerous psammoma bodies.Transcription factor EB (TFEB)-rearranged renal cell carcinoma is an even rarer entity, classically characterized by biphasic cellular morphology, rosette-like structures, and eosinophilic basement membrane-like material. Case Report:We describe a case of splicing factor proline-and glutamine-rich (SFPQ)/polypyrimidine tract-binding proteinassociated splicing factor (PSF)-TFE3 renal cell carcinoma confirmed by RNA sequencing that morphologically mimicked TFEB-rearranged renal cell carcinoma in a 66-year-old woman with concurrent high-grade urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder and ureter. Conclusions:This case expands the recognized histologic spectrum of TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma and highlights the critical role of molecular testing in establishing a definitive diagnosis.

records.title: Novel Triple-action Pt(IV) prodrugs with carbocyanine and chalcone in axial position: photoactivation, tumor targeting, fluorescent tumor visualization, and high therapeutic efficacy
records.abstract: Pt(IV) prodrugs are highly promising platform for anticancer agents due to the ability to fine-tune the structure and properties of the prodrug by varying the axial ligand conjugated with the Pt(IV) core. In this study, we have synthesized photoactivated Pt(IV) prodrugs with NIR-absorbing cyanine and chalcone in axial positions, which combine the advantages of dual-target chemotherapy, controlled photoactivation, photodynamic therapy, and fluorescent NIR bioimaging. The cyanine-chalcone-based prodrug Pt-4 demonstrated the ability to generate ROS, release carboplatin intracellularly and promote p53 expression under 660 nm light. Pt-4 prodrug demonstrated superior pharmacokinetic properties to carboplatin and excellent fluorescent imaging of CT-26 tumors. In vivo, Pt-4 prodrug + 660 nm light stimulated adaptive immune response in LLC tumors and significantly inhibited tumor growth of homograft CT-26 tumor. Our findings demonstrate excellent potential of Pt(IV)-carbocyanine light-activatable platform for tumor imaging, drug delivery and tumor eradication.

records.title: Brain tumor classification from contrast-enhanced T1 MRI, a patient-wise deep learning study
affiliations: Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology
records.abstract: Accurate classification of intracranial tumors on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1) is challenged by heterogeneous enhancement patterns and strong correlations among multiple slices from the same patient. We propose a compact CE-T1 MRI analysis framework that standardizes image intensities, enhances local CLAHE (contrast using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization), and applies a lightweight convolutional classifier whose slice-level probabilities are aggregated to obtain a single patient-level prediction. An independent optional U-Net-based pathway provides binary tumor segmentation when spatial delineation is required. Evaluation was performed using a strictly patient-wise, leakage-controlled protocol with stratified five-fold cross-validation on 233 subjects (3,064 slices) comprising glioma, meningioma, and pituitary adenoma. The classifier achieved 99.4% patient-level accuracy, with macro-averaged sensitivity and specificity of 99.3% and 99.0%, respectively. The optional segmentation pathway achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 97.3%. Post-hoc temperature scaling reduced the patient-level expected calibration error from 3.0% to approximately 1.2%, although larger independent cohorts are required to determine the stability of this estimate. records.title: Targeted delivery of therapeutic retroviral replicating vectors to glioma using adipose-derived stem cells
records.abstract: Abstract Gene delivery using retroviral replicating vectors (RRVs) is highly efficient, with nearly full transduction occurring throughout tumors in small-animal glioma models. However, vector spread is still restricted by the dosage that can be delivered by a single injection of viral vector supernatant, particularly in the large and diffusely infiltrating tumors that are characteristic of human high-grade gliomas. This study attempted to further improve the efficacy of this approach by engineering adult human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) to function as the carrier and producer cells for RRVs. We investigated the capability of RRV-producing hASCs (hASC-RRVs) to yield RRVs and deliver the vector to gliomas. The results show that RRVs released from hASC-RRVs can efficiently infect glioma cells, achieving tumor-selective and persistent gene delivery to gliomas. We have also confirmed the tumor-tropic migratory ability of hASC-RRVs, which greatly improved the efficiency of RRV delivery in vivo . In addition, the therapeutic effect of RRVs delivered by hASCs was increased markedly. In an orthotopic mouse model of human glioma, after a single injection of hASC-RRVs, hASC-RRV-mediated prodrug activator gene therapy resulted in chronic suppression of tumor growth and prolonged survival of the animals. Thus, using hASCs as the carrier and producer for RRVs may represent a promising strategy for glioma gene therapy.

affiliations: Third Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University
records.abstract: Protein kinases coordinate cellular proliferation, differentiation, survival, metabolism, and stress responses, and dysregulated kinase signalingf is a defining feature of many malignancies. From 2021 through 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) approved 26 small-molecule kinase inhibitors for cancer therapy, extending precision treatment across non-small-cell lung cancer, hematologic malignancies, breast and ovarian cancers, cholangiocarcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, glioma, and other kinase-driven tumors. The approved agents illustrate advances in medicinal chemistry and translational pharmacology that include covalent inhibitors such as sotorasib and futibatinib, mutation-selective inhibitors such as taletrectinib and zongertinib, allosteric inhibitors such as asciminib and mirdametinib, and multitarget or combination strategies such as avutometinib plus defactinib. Improvements in central nervous system exposure, mutant selectivity, dosing durability, and biomarker-defined patient selection have broadened clinical utility. This Review integrates the discovery background, mechanism of action, synthetic route, pharmacological properties, clinical efficacy, safety, and regulatory context of these agents. records.title: The TGF-β/ID1 Signaling Pathway Axis Mediates HPV E6/E7 Induced Malignant Transformation of Mammary Epithelial Cells
records.abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignancy among women worldwide. Increasing evidence implicates human papillomavirus (HPV) in breast cancer, particularly HPV16 and HPV18. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role of the TGF-β/ID1 signaling axis in HPV16/18 E6/E7 mediated malignant transformation of mammary epithelial cells. Stable MCF-10A cell lines expressing E6/E7 were established. E6/E7 expression promoted malignant transformation of mammary epithelial cells. RNA sequencing revealed extensive transcriptional reprogramming, with enrichment of cell cycle and DNA replication pathways. Gene set enrichment analysis and flow cytometry confirmed accelerated cell cycle progression, with increased S and G2/M phase populations. Mechanistically, E6/E7 upregulated TGFB2 and enhanced SMAD3 phosphorylation, indicating activation of canonical TGF-β signaling. TGFB2 silencing reduced SMAD3 activation and suppressed proliferation. E6/E7 also induced the downstream target ID1, whereas TGFB2 knockdown decreased ID1 expression. ID1 depletion inhibited proliferation and induced cell cycle arrest. In summary, E6/E7 promotes cell cycle progression and tumor initiating capacity via activation of the TGFB2–TGF-β–ID1 axis, providing mechanistic insight into HPV associated breast malignant transformation.
